mainTopic: אגדות on תהלים and prayer: ברוריה's lesson to pray for sinners to repent, סמוכים in תהלים, דוד's five 'ברכי נפשי', the soul compared to God, and חזקיהו's refusal to stop praying.
overview: This amud is a chain of אגדות, most of them explaining verses in תהלים. First the גמרא finishes proving that תהלים chapters 1 and 2 are one chapter, because a chapter דוד loved opens and closes with אשרי. Next comes the story of רבי מאיר and the hooligans who troubled him. His wife ברוריה showed from the words 'יתמו חטאים' that he should pray for their sins to end through תשובה, not for them to die. He did, and they repented. ברוריה also answers a מין who mocked 'רני עקרה'. Then רבי אבהו answers a מין about the order of chapters in תהלים: we learn from סמוכים, and placing אבשלום next to גוג ומגוג teaches that a rebellion against God is possible. The גמרא then lists the five 'worlds' in which דוד said 'ברכי נפשי', and gives a second explanation: five ways the נשמה is like הקדוש ברוך הוא. Finally, רב המנונא tells how God settled a dispute between חזקיהו and ישעיהו by making חזקיהו ill. ישעיהו told him he would die for neglecting פריה ורביה. חזקיהו refused to give up, quoting the rule that even with a sword on your neck you should never stop praying for mercy.

steps.title: Every chapter dear to דוד opens and closes with אשרי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states a rule: a chapter that was especially beloved to דוד both begins and ends with the word אשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every chapter that was dear to דוד, he opened it with 'אשרי' and closed it with 'אשרי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a general rule about how דוד wrote his most beloved chapters of תהלים: they start and end with אשרי. It is setting up a proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא claimed that 'אשרי האיש' (chapter 1) and 'למה רגשו גוים' (chapter 2) are really one single chapter. This rule is the tool for proving that claim. If a beloved chapter is framed by אשרי on both ends, then finding אשרי at the start of chapter 1 and the end of chapter 2 shows they form one unit.

keyTerms.meaning: A chapter or section (here, a chapter of תהלים)

phrases.aramaic: כָּל פָּרָשָׁה שֶׁהָיְתָה חֲבִיבָה עַל דָּוִד,
phrases.english: Every chapter that was dear to David,
he opened it with 'Ashrei'
and he concluded it with 'Ashrei.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּל פָּרָשָׁה שֶׁהָיְתָה חֲבִיבָה עַל דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof from the earlier part of the daf that תהלים chapters 1 and 2 form one chapter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד's beloved chapters are framed by אשרי at the beginning and at the end.

steps.title: The verses showing the opening and closing אשרי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the actual verses: 'אשרי האיש' opens chapter 1 and 'אשרי כל חוסי בו' closes chapter 2.
steps.simpleTranslation: He opened with 'אשרי,' as it is written: 'אשרי האיש' (Happy is the man). And he concluded with 'אשרי,' as it is written: 'אשרי כל חוסי בו' (Happy are all who take refuge in Him).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the two verses that prove the rule from the last step. It shows the opening אשרי and the closing אשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אשרי האיש' is the first verse of chapter 1. 'אשרי כל חוסי בו' is the last verse of chapter 2. Since the two אשרי's frame both chapters together, the two chapters must be one beloved unit.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who take refuge in Him

steps.whatToRemember: Chapters 1 and 2 of תהלים are treated as one chapter. The proof is that they open and close with אשרי, which is the sign of a chapter דוד loved.

phrases.english: He opened with 'Ashrei,' as it is written:
'Happy is the man.'
And he concluded with 'Ashrei,' as it is written:
'Happy are all who take refuge in Him.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 2:12, the last verse of chapter 2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural evidence for the rule stated in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That chapters 1 and 2 of תהלים form one chapter framed by אשרי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 1:1 ('אשרי האיש') and תהלים 2:12 ('אשרי כל חוסי בו').

steps.title: רבי מאיר prays that troublesome neighbors should die
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story: some hooligans near רבי מאיר troubled him greatly, so he prayed that they would die.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were certain hooligans in רבי מאיר's neighborhood, and they were causing him a lot of distress. רבי מאיר was praying for mercy concerning them, that they should die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story and sets the scene. רבי מאיר is suffering from bad neighbors and prays for their death. This sets up ברוריה's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story is linked to the verse 'יתמו חטאים מן הארץ', which was just used by רבי יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי about seeing the downfall of the wicked. רבי מאיר seems to understand that verse as permission to pray for the destruction of wicked people. The rest of the story will challenge that reading.

phrases.aramaic: הָנְהוּ בִּרְיוֹנֵי דַּהֲווֹ בְּשִׁבָבוּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.english: There were certain hooligans who were in Rabbi Meir's neighborhood
and they were causing him a great deal of distress.

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָא בָּעֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר רַחֲמֵי עִלָּוַיְהוּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir was praying for mercy concerning them
so that they would die.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ בִּרְיוֹנֵי דַּהֲווֹ בְּשִׁבָבוּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story tied to the verse 'יתמו חטאים', which the preceding teaching about הללויה used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup of the story: רבי מאיר prayed for the death of the wicked people tormenting him.

steps.title: ברוריה: the verse says 'sins,' not 'sinners'
steps.stepSummary: ברוריה challenges רבי מאיר's reading of 'יתמו חטאים'. The verse asks that sins should end, not sinners.
steps.simpleTranslation: ברוריה his wife said to him: What are you thinking? Is it because it is written 'Let חטאים cease'? Is it written 'חוטאים' (sinners)? It is written 'חטאים' (sins)!
steps.whatsHappening: ברוריה questions the basis of רבי מאיר's prayer. She argues that the verse he relies on is about ending sins, not ending sinners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She guesses his source is 'יתמו חטאים מן הארץ'. She then points out that the verse uses the word חטאים, which she reads as 'sins', instead of חוטאים, 'sinners'. So the verse is a request that wrongdoing should disappear, not that the people who do it should die.

keyTerms.meaning: ברוריה, רבי מאיר's wife, famous for her learning
What is your thinking? What is your basis?
Let them cease, come to an end

steps.confusionAlert: The word חטאים can also be read as 'sinners'. Compare 'רעים וחטאים' in בראשית 13:13. ברוריה is deliberately choosing to read it as 'sins'. Her second argument, in the next step, is what makes that reading stronger.

phrases.english: Berurya, his wife, said to him:
What is your thinking?
Is it because it is written, 'Let chata'im cease'?
Is it written 'sinners'?
'Sins' is written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the scriptural basis behind רבי מאיר's prayer in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's assumed reading of 'יתמו חטאים' as a call for the destruction of sinners.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Precise wording: the verse says חטאים (sins), not חוטאים (sinners), so it targets the wrongdoing, not the people.

steps.title: ברוריה's second argument from the end of the verse
steps.stepSummary: ברוריה adds a second proof from the end of the verse. If 'יתמו חטאים' meant the sinners die, then the words 'and the wicked will be no more' would add nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, look down to the end of the verse: 'And the wicked will be no more.' Once 'sins cease' (meaning the sinners are dead), why would it need to say 'and the wicked will be no more'?
steps.whatsHappening: ברוריה brings a second argument, this time from the end of the same verse. She asks a pointed question to show that רבי מאיר's reading makes the verse repeat itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first half of the verse meant the sinners would be wiped out, then the second half, 'ורשעים עוד אינם', would be pointless. The wicked would already be gone. So the first half must mean something different from the second half.

keyTerms.meaning: Go down to the end of the verse
And the wicked will be no more

phrases.english: And furthermore, go down to the end of the verse:
'And the wicked will be no more.'
Once 'sins cease' (in your reading, the sinners die),
[why say] 'and the wicked will be no more'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent argument supporting ברוריה's reading from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That 'יתמו חטאים' cannot mean the death of sinners.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of תהלים 104:35, 'ורשעים עוד אינם', which would be redundant under רבי מאיר's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's reading of 'יתמו חטאים' as the death of sinners.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: if the first half already means the sinners die, the second half 'ורשעים עוד אינם' would add nothing.

steps.title: ברוריה's alternative: pray that they do תשובה
steps.stepSummary: ברוריה gives the correct reading and the correct prayer. Pray that they do תשובה. Then their sins end, and they are no longer 'wicked'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, pray for mercy for them, that they should return in repentance, and then 'the wicked will be no more.'
steps.whatsHappening: After knocking down רבי מאיר's reading, ברוריה offers the right one. He should pray that the hooligans do תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reading makes both halves of the verse work. First the sins stop. As a result, the people are no longer רשעים, even though they are still alive. 'The wicked will be no more' now means they stop being wicked, not that they stop existing.

keyTerms.meaning: That they should return in repentance

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the idea that one should pray for the wicked to do תשובה rather than for their destruction. The goal is to remove the sin, not the sinner.

phrases.english: Rather, pray for mercy for them
that they should return in repentance,
[and then] 'the wicked will be no more.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the verse-reading problem raised in steps 4 and 5 with a positive interpretation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יתמו חטאים' calls for the death of sinners, so one may pray for it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse calls for the end of sin through תשובה. Once they repent, they are no longer רשעים.

steps.title: רבי מאיר prays for them and they repent
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר accepts ברוריה's argument and prays for the hooligans to repent, and they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: He prayed for mercy for them, and they returned in repentance.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רבי מאיר follows his wife's advice and prays that they do תשובה, and the prayer works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's actions show that he accepted ברוריה's reading. The successful result confirms that praying for תשובה was the right approach.
steps.whatToRemember: ברוריה's lesson: 'יתמו חטאים', not חוטאים. Pray that the sins end through תשובה, not that the sinners die. רבי מאיר did so, and the hooligans repented.

phrases.english: He prayed for mercy for them,
and they returned in repentance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי מאיר acting on ברוריה's advice from step 6, and the result.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Praying for the wicked to repent is the correct reading of 'יתמו חטאים', and it is effective. The hooligans did תשובה.

steps.title: A heretic mocks the verse 'Sing, barren woman'
steps.stepSummary: A מין challenges ברוריה: the verse tells a barren woman to sing, but why should anyone rejoice over not having children?
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain heretic said to ברוריה: It is written, 'Sing, barren woman who has not given birth.' Because she did not give birth, she should sing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second story about ברוריה. A מין attacks a verse in ישעיה because it seems to make no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not having children was seen as a great sorrow. So a verse telling a barren woman to sing for joy looks illogical, and the מין uses it to mock the נביא. This sets up ברוריה's answer in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A heretic, someone who rejected the Torah and often mocked its verses

phrases.english: A certain heretic said to Beruria:
It is written: 'Sing, barren woman who has not given birth'
Because she has not given birth, she should sing?!
phrases.notes: A mocking question, not a real request for information

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story that shows ברוריה's skill in reading verses, following the story of her and רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The verse 'רני עקרה לא ילדה' in ישעיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Childlessness is a cause for sadness, so telling a barren woman to rejoice seems absurd.

steps.title: ברוריה points to the end of the verse
steps.stepSummary: ברוריה calls the מין a fool and tells him to read the end of the verse, which says the 'desolate' woman will have more children than the married one.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: Fool! Look at the end of the verse, where it is written: 'For the children of the desolate will be more than the children of the married woman, says ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: ברוריה begins her answer by showing that the verse itself proves the מין misread it. This is the proof she builds on before she gives the real meaning in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the verse says the 'barren' woman will actually have many children. So the verse cannot be praising simple childlessness. 'Barren' must be a picture of something else. This is the same method she used with רבי מאיר: read the whole verse, not just the start.

keyTerms.meaning: Look down, go down (to a later part of the text)

phrases.english: She said to him: Fool!
Go down to the end of the verse, where it is written:
'For more are the children of the desolate one
than the children of the married woman, says ה׳.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer the מין's challenge by using the end of the same verse.
steps.raayaObject: That 'barren woman' in the verse is not about real childlessness
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the verse: 'כי רבים בני שוממה מבני בעולה'

steps.title: The barren woman is the Jewish people
steps.stepSummary: ברוריה explains that the 'barren woman' is כנסת ישראל, who rejoices because she did not give birth to children destined for גיהנום like the מין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'barren woman who has not given birth' mean? Sing, כנסת ישראל, who is like a barren woman because she did not give birth to children destined for גיהנום, like you.
steps.whatsHappening: ברוריה gives the true meaning of the verse and turns the mockery back on the מין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'barrenness' is not a lack of children. It is a lack of wicked children. כנסת ישראל rejoices that she has no children like the מין, and in the end she will have many children. This answers the challenge and also rebukes the questioner.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what does it mean? (introduces the correct explanation)
The community of Israel, the Jewish people as a whole
The place of punishment for the wicked

steps.whatToRemember: ברוריה reads the whole verse in context. 'Barren' means Israel has no children like the heretics, so she sings for joy.

phrases.english: Rather, what is the meaning of 'barren woman who has not given birth'?
Sing, congregation of Israel,
which is like a barren woman
who did not give birth to children destined for Gehinnom, like you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes ברוריה's answer by giving the correct reading that the proof in step 9 pointed to.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse praises a woman for having no children at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse praises כנסת ישראל for not producing wicked children like the מין.

steps.title: Why is the אבשלום מזמור placed before the שאול מזמור?
steps.stepSummary: A מין asks רבי אבהו: the מזמור about דוד fleeing אבשלום comes before the one about fleeing שאול, but the שאול story happened first, so it should have been written first.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain heretic said to רבי אבהו: It is written, 'A psalm of דוד, when he fled from his son אבשלום,' and it is written, 'Of דוד, a מכתם, when he fled from שאול into the cave.' Which event happened first? Since the שאול event happened first, it should have been written first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story. A מין points to what looks like a wrong order in תהלים. This step sets up רבי אבהו's answer, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fleeing from שאול happened when דוד was young, long before אבשלום rebelled. Yet the אבשלום psalm is chapter 3 and the שאול psalm is chapter 57. The מין claims the order of תהלים is careless.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of psalm, a heading word in תהלים
Since, after all (introduces an obvious premise)
Let it write, it should have written

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the מין is asking which story happened first. He already knows the שאול story came first. His real point is that תהלים seems to be in the wrong order.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ,
phrases.english: A certain heretic said to Rabbi Abbahu:
It is written: 'A psalm of David
when he fled from his son Absalom'
and it is written: 'Of David, a mikhtam,
when he fled from Saul into the cave.'
Which event happened first?
Since the event with Saul happened first,
it should have been written first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new exchange with a מין. It moves from ישעיה to the order of chapters in תהלים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the chapters in תהלים (chapter 3 before chapter 57)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Events should be recorded in the order they happened. The שאול flight came first, so placing it later suggests the order of תהלים is wrong.

steps.title: רבי אבהו says the order is no problem for those who learn from סמוכים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו tells the מין that the question only bothers someone who does not learn from סמוכים. Since we do learn from them, the order is deliberate and teaches a lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For you, who don't learn from verses placed next to each other, this is difficult. For us, who do learn from verses placed next to each other, it is not difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the מין's challenge about why the אבשלום מזמור comes before the שאול מזמור. He says the order is not by time. Verses are placed next to each other on purpose, to teach something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מין assumed תהלים must follow the order in which events happened. רבי אבהו rejects that assumption: placement can be meant to teach a lesson, not to record a timeline. He has not yet said what the lesson is. That comes in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: Juxtapositions: learning a lesson from two passages placed next to each other

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבהו is not saying the שאול story happened later. He agrees it happened first. He is saying the book is arranged for teaching, not by date.

phrases.english: He (Rabbi Abbahu) said to him:
You, who do not expound juxtapositions,
it is difficult for you.
We, who do expound juxtapositions,
it is not difficult for us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן דְּלָא דָּרְשִׁיתוּן סְמוּכִין קַשְׁיָא לְכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מין's challenge from step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the assumption that the order must follow time; the placement is meant to teach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מזמורים should follow the order in which the events happened
steps.terutzMaskana: The order is deliberate, because we learn lessons from juxtaposed passages

steps.title: Scriptural source for learning from juxtaposition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a פסוק showing that סמוכים is a real method rooted in Scripture.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: From where in Scripture do we know we learn from juxtapositions? As it says: 'Adjoined forever and ever, made in truth and uprightness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי אבהו's method by showing that it comes from a פסוק. It is not just an idea he made up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים describes God's commandments as 'סמוכים', placed side by side. That wording is read as a sign that their placement next to each other is meaningful and done 'in truth'. This gives the method of step 12 a textual basis.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introducing a פסוק)

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
From where in Scripture do we derive juxtapositions?
As it is said:
"Adjoined forever and ever,
made in truth and uprightness."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סְמוּכִין מִן הַתּוֹרָה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the scriptural basis for the method רבי אבהו relied on
steps.raayaObject: That learning from סמוכים is a valid method
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים קי״א: סמוכים לעד לעולם עשוים באמת וישר

steps.title: The lesson of placing אבשלום next to גוג ומגוג
steps.stepSummary: The אבשלום מזמור is placed next to the גוג ומגוג מזמור to show that an unthinkable rebellion can really happen. If a son rebelled against his father, people can also rebel against God.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why was the chapter of אבשלום placed next to the chapter of גוג ומגוג? So that if someone says to you, 'Is there a slave who rebels against his master?!', you can answer him, 'Is there a son who rebels against his father?' Yet it happened, so here too it will happen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the actual lesson that explains the order of the מזמורים. This completes רבי אבהו's answer to the מין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might doubt the prophecy that the nations of גוג ומגוג will rebel against God and His anointed: how could servants rebel against their Master? The answer points to אבשלום, a son who rebelled against his own father דוד. That also seems impossible, yet it truly happened. So placing the two side by side proves the rebellion of גוג ומגוג is possible too.

keyTerms.meaning: The nations who will wage war against God at the end of days (תהלים ב׳)

steps.whatToRemember: The order of the מזמורים teaches a lesson, not a timeline. אבשלום's rebellion against his father proves that the 'impossible' rebellion of גוג ומגוג against God can happen.
steps.confusionAlert: The juxtaposition here is between the אבשלום מזמור (chapter 3) and the מזמור before it about גוג ומגוג (chapter 2, 'למה רגשו גוים'). It is not about the שאול מזמור.

phrases.english: Why was the chapter of Absalom juxtaposed
with the chapter of Gog and Magog?
So that if a person says to you:
Is there a slave who rebels against his master?!
You too say to him:
Is there a son who rebels against his father?
Yet it happened;
here too it will happen.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נִסְמְכָה פָּרָשַׁת אַבְשָׁלוֹם לְפָרָשַׁת גּוֹג וּמָגוֹג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the סמוכים method to explain the specific order the מין asked about
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the concrete lesson behind the juxtaposition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אבשלום מזמור is out of chronological order with no reason
steps.terutzMaskana: It is placed next to גוג ומגוג to prove that a rebellion against God is possible
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a basic way the גמרא reads תנ״ך: placement and order can carry meaning beyond the plain story.

steps.title: שלמה's verse 'פיה פתחה בחכמה' refers to דוד
steps.stepSummary: A new teaching begins. רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, explains that שלמה said 'פיה פתחה בחכמה' about his father דוד, who lived in five 'worlds' and said שירה in each.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: What is meant by the verse 'She opens her mouth with wisdom, and the teaching of kindness is on her tongue'? About whom did שלמה say this verse? He said it only about his father דוד, who lived in five worlds and said song.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new aggadic section by explaining a פסוק in משלי. It identifies דוד as the one who 'opens his mouth with wisdom'. This also sets up the next part, which will list the five 'worlds'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to describe the אשת חיל, but it is read as praise of דוד. The reason is that דוד sang praise to God in every stage of his existence. The 'five worlds' are named here but not yet spelled out. The גמרא will go on to list them and match each one to a 'ברכי נפשי'.

keyTerms.meaning: What is meant by what is written?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"She opens her mouth with wisdom,
and the teaching of kindness is on her tongue"?

phrases.aramaic: כְּנֶגֶד מִי אָמַר שְׁלֹמֹה מִקְרָא זֶה? —
phrases.english: With reference to whom did Solomon say this verse?

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֲמָרוֹ אֶלָּא כְּנֶגֶד דָּוִד אָבִיו,
phrases.english: He said it only about his father David,
who dwelled in five worlds
and said song.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new aggadic teaching, separate from the מין discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'פיה פתחה בחכמה' was said by שלמה about דוד, who sang שירה in each of the five worlds he lived in

steps.title: The first world: דוד sang in his mother's womb
steps.stepSummary: While still in his mother's womb, דוד said שירה, using the words 'בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי אֶת ה׳ וְכָל קְרָבַי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He lived in his mother's womb and said a song, as it says: 'Bless God, O my soul, and all that is within me, His holy name.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins listing the five worlds promised in step 15. The first world is the womb, and the פסוק is read as a song from inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'וְכָל קְרָבַי' (all my inner parts) are read as being about the inside of the mother, meaning the womb. So the פסוק becomes praise for how God forms a baby inside the womb.

keyTerms.meaning: in his mother's womb (literally, 'in his mother's insides')
a song of praise to God
my inner parts. Here it is read as the womb.

phrases.english: He dwelt in his mother's womb
and said a song, as it is stated:
'Bless the Lord, O my soul,'
'and all that is within me, His holy name.'
phrases.notes: 'Within me' is read as the womb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts filling in the list of five worlds that step 15 introduced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the womb, דוד praised God for forming the baby inside the mother, based on 'וְכָל קְרָבַי'.

steps.title: The second world: דוד was born and sang about the stars
steps.stepSummary: When דוד came out into the world and saw the stars and constellations, he said 'בָּרְכוּ ה׳ מַלְאָכָיו... כָּל צְבָאָיו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came out into the open air of the world, looked at the stars and constellations, and said a song, as it says: 'Bless God, His angels, mighty in strength, who do His word, listening to the voice of His word. Bless God, all His hosts, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second world: life outside the womb. Seeing the huge heavens, דוד praised God as the One whom all of creation serves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All His hosts' (צבאיו) is read as the stars and heavenly bodies. However great they look, they are servants doing God's will. That is why seeing the sky leads to praising God rather than the stars.

keyTerms.meaning: into the open air of the world, meaning he was born
His hosts. Here this means the heavenly bodies.

phrases.english: He emerged into the air of the world
and looked at the stars and constellations
and said a song, as it is stated:
'Bless the Lord, His angels, mighty in strength,'
'who fulfill His word, listening to the voice of His word;'
'Bless the Lord, all His hosts, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצָא לַאֲוִיר הָעוֹלָם וְנִסְתַּכֵּל בְּכוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item on the list of worlds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At birth, seeing the heavens, דוד praised God as the One served by all the heavenly hosts.

steps.title: The third world: דוד nursed and sang
steps.stepSummary: While nursing, דוד looked at his mother's breasts and said 'בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי אֶת ה׳ וְאַל תִּשְׁכְּחִי כָּל גְּמוּלָיו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He nursed from his mother's breasts, looked at them, and said a song, as it says: 'Bless God, O my soul, and do not forget all His benefits.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third world: infancy and nursing. The פסוק that mentions 'גמוליו' is tied to nursing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גְּמוּלָיו sounds like 'גְּמוּלֵי חָלָב', which means babies weaned from milk. So the פסוק is read as thanks for the gift of nursing. This connection sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: His benefits. It is connected to nursing and weaning (גְּמוּלֵי חָלָב).

phrases.english: He nursed from his mother's breasts
and looked at her breasts
and said a song, as it is stated:
'Bless the Lord, O my soul,'
'and do not forget all His benefits.'
phrases.notes: גמוליו is linked to nursing and weaning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third item on the list of worlds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While nursing, דוד praised God for the gift of nursing, based on 'כָּל גְּמוּלָיו'.

steps.title: What is special about 'all His benefits'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly 'כָּל גְּמוּלָיו' refers to. What is so praiseworthy about how God set up nursing?
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'all His benefits' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask a clarifying question about the פסוק it just quoted. This sets up רבי אבהו's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every animal nurses its young, so just feeding the baby does not explain the special praise. The question asks for the specific kindness that דוד noticed and praised.

keyTerms.meaning: what is it? (asks for an explanation)

phrases.english: What is 'all His benefits'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the precise meaning of the פסוק quoted in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What specific kindness of God is meant by 'כָּל גְּמוּלָיו' in connection with nursing.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: God placed the breasts near the heart
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that God placed the mother's breasts at the place of understanding, near the heart, and not lower on the body as with most animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: That He made her breasts at the place of understanding.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question from step 19. The special kindness is where God placed the nursing place on the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heart was seen as the seat of understanding (בינה). In most animals, the nursing place is low on the body. In a human mother, God placed it up by the heart, and that dignified placement is the 'benefit' דוד praised.

keyTerms.meaning: at the place of understanding, meaning the heart

steps.whatToRemember: The first three worlds of דוד are: (1) the womb, (2) birth and seeing the heavens, (3) nursing. Each came with its own שירה from תהלים ק״ג. 'כל גמוליו' refers to God placing the breasts at the 'place of understanding', the heart.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
That He made breasts for her
at the place of understanding.
phrases.notes: The heart, considered the seat of understanding.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ שֶׁעָשָׂה לָהּ דַּדִּים בִּמְקוֹם בִּינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כל גמוליו' refers to God placing the breasts at the place of understanding (the heart), unlike in most animals.

steps.title: Why did God place nursing near the heart?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason God placed a mother's breasts near the heart rather than lower down.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about רבי אבהו's point. Why did God put the place of nursing up near the heart? This question sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו told us what God did, but not why it matters. The גמרא now wants the purpose behind the design, since that purpose is what makes it a 'גְּמוּל', a kindness worth praising.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Asking why God placed the breasts near the heart (step 20).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the purpose behind רבי אבהו's description in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of placing the nursing area near the heart.

steps.title: רב יהודה: so the baby won't look at an immodest place
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says the purpose is so the nursing child will not look at the place of ערוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: So that he should not look at the place of nakedness.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the first answer. The breasts are placed high up so the nursing baby will not be looking at his mother's private area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's answer is about modesty. Lower down, the child would be facing an immodest place. God's design protects the child from that, and this is a kindness worth praising.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
So that he (the baby) should not look at the place of nakedness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The purpose is modesty: the child does not gaze at the place of ערוה.

steps.title: רב מתנא: so the baby won't nurse from an unclean place
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנא gives a different reason: so the child will not nurse from a place of filth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנא said: So that he should not nurse from a place of filth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנא gives a second answer. The breasts are placed high so the baby will not be nursing near the body's place of waste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה focused on what the child sees, which is about modesty. רב מתנא focuses on cleanliness, so the child is not fed near a dirty area. Both agree on what God did and only explain the benefit differently.

keyTerms.meaning: A place of filth (where waste leaves the body)

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
So that he should not nurse from a place of filth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative answer to the same question, next to רב יהודה's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The purpose is cleanliness: the child does not nurse from a place of filth.

steps.title: Fourth time: seeing the downfall of the wicked
steps.stepSummary: דוד saw the wicked fall and said שירה, using a verse that ends with 'בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw the downfall of the wicked and said a song, as it says: 'Let sinners cease from the earth, and the wicked be no more. Bless the Lord, O my soul, הללויה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The list moves on to the fourth time דוד said 'בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי'. This time it was when he saw the wicked being destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each stage of the list is a new moment in דוד's life, matched to a verse with the words 'בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי'. Here the verse itself talks about sinners ending and then says 'בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי', so the link is easy to see.

keyTerms.meaning: A song of praise to God
Let sins/sinners come to an end

phrases.english: He saw the downfall of the wicked,
and said a song, as it is said:
"Let sinners cease from the earth,
and let the wicked be no more;
Bless the Lord, O my soul, Halleluyah."

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאָה בְּמַפַּלְתָּן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים, וְאָמַר שִׁירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side question about nursing, the גמרא goes back to the list of five 'בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי' moments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fourth 'בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי' was said on seeing the downfall of the wicked.

steps.title: Fifth time: looking at the day of death
steps.stepSummary: דוד looked at the day of death and said שירה, using the opening verse of תהלים 104.
steps.simpleTranslation: He looked at the day of death and said a song, as it says: 'Bless the Lord, O my soul; Lord my God, You are very great, You are clothed in glory and majesty.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the fifth and last time דוד said 'בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי'. It was when he thought about the day of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This verse says nothing about death on the surface. It only praises God's greatness. That gap is exactly what leads the גמרא to ask a question in the next step.

phrases.english: He looked upon the day of death,
and said a song, as it is said:
"Bless the Lord, O my soul;
Lord my God, You are very great;
You are clothed in glory and majesty."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with the fifth and final moment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fifth 'בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי' was said when דוד looked at the day of death.

steps.title: How do we know this verse is about death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what shows that the verse 'ה׳ אֱלֹהַי גָּדַלְתָּ מְּאֹד' was said about the day of death.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is it implied that it was said about the day of death?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know the verse from step 25 is about death, since it doesn't mention death at all. This question sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier stages, the verse matched the moment clearly. For example, the verse about the wicked actually mentions the wicked. Here the verse only praises God, so the גמרא wants a textual basis for tying it to death.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is it implied? How do we see this?

phrases.english: From where is it implied
that it was said about the day of death?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּעַל יוֹם הַמִּיתָה נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the link between the verse and the day of death from step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A textual source showing that תהלים 104:1 relates to death.

steps.title: רבה בר רב שילא: the end of the same מזמור speaks of death
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא proves it from later in the same chapter, which describes creatures dying when God hides His face.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב שילא said: From the end of the passage, as it is written: 'You hide Your face, they are terrified; You gather their breath, they perish, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב שילא answers that later in the same chapter of תהלים, the verses talk about death. So the whole chapter, including its opening 'בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי', is connected to death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by reading the chapter as one unit. Its opening praise is understood in light of its ending, where God takes away the breath of living things and they die. So 'You are very great' is דוד's praise of God even when he looks at death.
steps.whatToRemember: דוד said 'בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי' five times: in the womb, on coming into the world, while nursing, on seeing the downfall of the wicked, and on the day of death. The last one is tied to death because the end of תהלים 104 describes dying.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Sheila said:
From the end of the passage, as it is written:
"You hide Your face, they are terrified;
You gather in their breath, they perish, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא, מִסֵּיפָא דְעִנְיָינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26 and closes the list of five.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The end of the same psalm (104:29) describes death, so the psalm's opening praise refers to the day of death.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All five 'בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי' moments are now explained, with the fifth tied to death through the end of תהלים 104.

steps.title: Introducing the conversation: a student and an aggadah expert
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces רב שימי בר עוקבא, who used to learn before רבי שמעון בן פזי. רבי שמעון בן פזי was the one who organized אגדה before רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר עוקבא (some say מר עוקבא) used to spend time learning before רבי שמעון בן פזי, who would arrange אגדה before רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting the scene for a new conversation about the verse ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי״. Nothing is taught yet. It only tells us who is talking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects back to step 16, where the verse ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי... וְכָל קְרָבַי״ was explained as דוד's song in the womb. Now a new approach to the same verse begins. We are told that רבי שמעון בן פזי is an expert in אגדה, which signals that the discussion will be a deep explanation of the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Was regularly found before him (studied with him often)
And some say (an alternate version of the name)

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ukva
and some say Mar Ukva,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה שְׁכִיחַ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי,
phrases.english: was regularly found before Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi,
who would arrange aggadah
phrases.notes: Following רש״י, the one arranging אגדה is רבי שמעון בן פזי.

phrases.english: before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Narrative setup (could be merged with the question that follows)
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר עוּקְבָא וְאָמְרִי לַהּ מָר עוּקְבָא הֲוָה שְׁכִיחַ קַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story that gives another explanation of ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי... וְכָל קְרָבַי״, the verse quoted in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up who is speaking: a student, רב שימי, and an aggadah master, רבי שמעון בן פזי.

steps.title: What does 'Bless God, my soul, and all my insides' mean?
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי asks רבי שמעון בן פזי to explain the verse ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי אֶת ה׳ וְכָל קְרָבַי אֶת שֵׁם קָדְשׁוֹ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is the meaning of what is written, 'Bless God, my soul, and all my insides, His holy name'?
steps.whatsHappening: The student asks his teacher for the meaning of a verse in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is open-ended. It is not yet clear what exactly he wants to know. The teacher will first explain why the 'insides' (קרבי) praise God. Later, in step 34, the student will clarify that he meant something more specific.

keyTerms.meaning: What is [the meaning of] what is written

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase ״אֲמַר לֵיהּ״ (he said to him) repeats several times in this story without names. Here the student רב שימי asks. In the next step, the teacher רבי שמעון בן פזי answers.

phrases.english: He said to him:
What is [the meaning of] that which is written,
'Bless the Lord, my soul,
and all my insides, His holy name'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מַאי דִּכְתִיב בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי אֶת ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The conversation introduced in step 28 begins with this question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the verse ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי אֶת ה׳ וְכָל קְרָבַי אֶת שֵׁם קָדְשׁוֹ״.

steps.title: God draws a form inside a form and gives it life
steps.stepSummary: A human can paint a picture on a wall but cannot give it a soul or inner organs. God forms a baby inside its mother and gives it a spirit, a soul, and insides.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Come and see that God's way is not like the way of people. A person draws a picture on a wall but cannot put into it a spirit, a soul, or inner organs. God is not like that. He forms a shape inside a shape and puts into it a spirit, a soul, and inner organs.
steps.whatsHappening: The teacher answers that the verse praises God for creating a living person, inside and out, within the mother's womb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why the verse mentions ״קְרָבַי״, the insides. A human artist only makes a flat outside image. God makes the inner organs and breathes in a soul, and He does it hidden inside another body ('a form within a form'). So the soul and the insides have a reason to bless Him.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and see (an opening formula for a teaching)
The way of flesh and blood (human beings)
A form inside a form (a baby inside its mother)

phrases.english: He said to him: Come and see
that not like the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the way of flesh and blood.
The way of flesh and blood: he draws a form
on the wall,
and he cannot put into it
spirit and soul, insides and intestines.
But the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not so;
He forms a form within a form
and puts into it spirit and soul,
insides and intestines.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The soul and insides bless God because He alone forms a living being inside its mother, complete with soul and organs. A human artist can only paint a lifeless outer image.

steps.title: Support from חנה's song
steps.stepSummary: The same idea is found in חנה's words after שמואל was born: ״אֵין קָדוֹשׁ כַּה׳ כִּי אֵין בִּלְתֶּךָ וְאֵין צוּר כֵּאלֹהֵינוּ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what חנה said: 'There is none holy like God, for there is none besides You, and there is no rock like our God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The teacher brings a verse from חנה's prayer to back up his idea about God forming a baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנה said this right after giving birth, so her praise fits the theme of God forming a child in the womb. The next two steps will explain two phrases from this verse in a new way.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is [what is meant by]

phrases.english: And this is what Hannah said:
'There is none holy like the Lord,
for there is none besides You,
and there is no rock like our God.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the teaching of step 30 with a verse.
steps.raayaObject: That God is the unique 'artist' who forms life inside the womb.
steps.raayaSupportSource: חנה's song after the birth of שמואל (שמואל א ב:ב).

steps.title: 'No rock like our God' means 'no artist like our God'
steps.stepSummary: The word צוּר (rock) is read as צַיָּיר (artist): no one can form things the way God does.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'there is no rock like our God' mean? There is no artist like our God.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how חנה's verse proves the point. It reads the word צוּר as if it meant 'artist'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word צוּר sounds like צָר (forms/draws) from step 30. So 'no צוּר like our God' becomes 'no one who forms like our God'. That is exactly the idea of God forming a baby inside its mother.

phrases.english: What is 'there is no rock like our God'?
There is no artist like our God.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה (the question and answer are combined in one line)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the verse quoted in step 31 supports step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: צוּר is read as צַיָּיר: God is the incomparable artist.

steps.title: 'None besides You' read as 'none can outlast You'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר מנסיא reads ״אֵין בִּלְתֶּךָ״ as ״אֵין לְבַלּוֹתֶךָ״. A person's creations outlast him, but God outlasts His creations.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'for there is none besides You' mean? רבי יהודה בר מנסיא said: Do not read it 'there is none besides You'; read it 'there is none to outlast You'. God's way is not like the way of people. People's handiwork outlasts them, but God outlasts His handiwork.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the other phrase in חנה's verse, using a new reading of the word בִּלְתֶּךָ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using an ״אַל תִּקְרֵי״ reading, בִּלְתֶּךָ is connected to the root בלה, 'to wear out'. Normally a builder dies and his building is still standing. God is the reverse: He outlives everything He makes. This is a second way God is unlike a human craftsman.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read [the word as] ... but rather [as] (a reading-based דרשה)
To wear You out / outlast You

steps.confusionAlert: ״אַל תִּקְרֵי״ does not mean the written text is changed. It adds an extra layer of meaning on top of the plain reading.

phrases.english: What is 'for there is none besides You'?
Rabbi Yehuda bar Menasya said:
Do not read 'for there is none besides You,'
but rather 'there is none to outlast You.'
For not like the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the way of flesh and blood:
The way of flesh and blood:
the work of his hands outlasts him,
but the Holy One, Blessed be He, outlasts His works.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי כִּי אֵין בִּלְתֶּךָ אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר מְנַסְיָא אַל תִּקְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second phrase of the verse from step 31, parallel to how step 32 explained the first.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בִּלְתֶּךָ is read as לְבַלּוֹתֶךָ: nothing outlasts God, while human creations outlast their makers.

steps.title: The student clarifies: whom do the five 'Bless God, my soul' correspond to?
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי says he meant a different question: דוד said ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי״ five times, so what are those five times about?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I was asking you: these five times of 'Bless God, my soul', about whom did דוד say them?
steps.whatsHappening: The student says the answer missed his real question. He restates it more precisely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer explained what one verse means. The student wanted to know why the phrase appears five times, and what the soul is being compared to each time. This moves the discussion from one verse to a pattern across תהלים.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I was saying to you (I meant this)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, אֲנָא הָכִי קָא אָמֵינָא לָךְ:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I was saying to you:
these five 'Bless, my soul' —
corresponding to whom did David say them?

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: דחיה (it implicitly sets aside the previous answer as off-target)
steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אֲנָא הָכִי קָא אָמֵינָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refocuses the original question of step 29, since the answer in steps 30-33 did not address what the student meant.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the five occurrences of ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי״ correspond to.

steps.title: They correspond to God and to the soul
steps.stepSummary: דוד said the five ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי״ about הקדוש ברוך הוא and the נשמה, comparing the soul in the body to God in the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said them only about the Holy One, Blessed be He, and about the soul.
steps.whatsHappening: The teacher answers the clarified question: each ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי״ is a comparison between God and the soul.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The soul blesses God because it resembles Him. The soul relates to the body the way God relates to the world. The five times the phrase appears match five such similarities, which the גמרא will spell out next.
steps.whatToRemember: The five ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי״ are parallels between God and the soul. Like God, the soul has qualities that make it fit to praise Him. The details of the five come next.

phrases.english: He said them only
corresponding to the Holy One, Blessed be He,
and corresponding to the soul.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא אֲמָרָן אֶלָּא כְּנֶגֶד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וּכְנֶגֶד נְשָׁמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refocused question of step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The five ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי״ were said about God and the soul, setting up a comparison between them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the famous list of five ways the soul is like God, which the גמרא develops in the next step.

steps.title: Five ways the soul is like God
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists five parallels between הקדוש ברוך הוא in the world and the נשמה in the body. Both fill everything, see without being seen, sustain, are pure, and dwell in the innermost place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as God fills the whole world, the soul fills the whole body. Just as God sees but cannot be seen, the soul sees but cannot be seen. Just as God feeds the whole world, the soul feeds the whole body. Just as God is pure, the soul is pure. Just as God dwells in the innermost chambers, the soul dwells in the innermost chambers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the five comparisons it promised in the last step. Each one matches one of דוד's five ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 35 only said that the five ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי״ are about God and the soul. Here we get the actual content: five specific traits the two share. Each line uses the same pattern: ״מָה... אַף...״ (just as... so too...).

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too... (a formula for making a comparison)
In the innermost rooms (a hidden, inner place)

phrases.aramaic: מָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָלֵא כָּל הָעוֹלָם —
phrases.english: Just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, fills the entire world —

phrases.aramaic: אַף נְשָׁמָה מְלֵאָה אֶת כָּל הַגּוּף.
phrases.english: so too the soul fills the entire body.

phrases.aramaic: מָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רוֹאֶה וְאֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה —
phrases.english: Just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, sees but is not seen —
so too the soul sees but is not seen.

phrases.aramaic: מָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא זָן אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ —
phrases.english: Just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, sustains the entire world —

phrases.aramaic: אַף נְשָׁמָה זָנָה אֶת כָּל הַגּוּף.
phrases.english: so too the soul sustains the entire body.
Just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, is pure —
so too the soul is pure.

phrases.aramaic: מָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹשֵׁב בְּחַדְרֵי חֲדָרִים —
phrases.english: Just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, dwells in a chamber within a chamber —
so too the soul dwells in a chamber within a chamber.
phrases.notes: In the innermost part of the body.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָלֵא כָּל הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the details of step 35's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The five ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי״ match five traits shared by God and the soul.

steps.title: The soul with five traits should praise the God with five traits
steps.stepSummary: The conclusion: the נשמה, which has these five traits, should praise הקדוש ברוך הוא, who has the same five traits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the one who has these five qualities come and praise the One Who has these five qualities.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the five comparisons. This is why דוד's soul praises God five times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line explains why the comparison matters. Because the soul mirrors God in five ways, it is fitting for the soul to praise Him. That closes the answer to the question about the five ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי״.
steps.whatToRemember: The five ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי״ match five ways the soul is like God. Like God, the soul fills, sees without being seen, sustains, is pure, and is hidden, so the soul praises its Creator.

phrases.aramaic: יָבֹא מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה דְבָרִים הַלָּלוּ
phrases.english: Let the one who has these five characteristics come

phrases.aramaic: וִישַׁבֵּחַ לְמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה דְבָרִים הַלָּלוּ.
phrases.english: and praise the One Who has these five characteristics.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָבֹא מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה דְבָרִים הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the five comparisons.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The soul, which mirrors God in five ways, should praise Him. This explains the five ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי״.

steps.title: God makes a compromise between two righteous men
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא reads the verse ״מִי כְּהֶחָכָם וּמִי יוֹדֵעַ פֵּשֶׁר דָּבָר״ as praise of God. He knows how to make a פשרה between two צדיקים, חזקיהו and ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: What does the verse mean, 'Who is like the wise one, and who knows the explanation of a matter'? It means: Who is like God, Who knows how to make a compromise between two righteous people, between חזקיהו and ישעיהו?
steps.whatsHappening: A new aggadic section begins. רב המנונא explains a verse and sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא connects the word פֵּשֶׁר (explanation) to פְּשָׁרָה (compromise). The 'wise one' is God, Who can settle a dispute between two righteous people. This line introduces the dispute, which the next steps describe.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written (introduces a verse to explain)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a brand-new topic, not a continuation of the soul discussion. Don't look for a link to the five ״בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי״.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
'Who is like the wise man, and who knows the interpretation of a matter' (Kohelet 8:1)?
Who is like the Holy One, Blessed be He,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לַעֲשׂוֹת פְּשָׁרָה בֵּין שְׁנֵי צַדִּיקִים,
phrases.english: Who knows how to make a compromise between two righteous people,
between Hezekiah and Isaiah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new aggadic topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse praises God's ability to make peace between two righteous people, חזקיהו and ישעיהו.

steps.title: חזקיהו's claim: the prophet should come to the king
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו argued that ישעיהו should come to him. His proof was that אליהו the prophet went to King אחאב.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיהו said: Let ישעיהו come to me. That is what we find with אליהו, who went to אחאב, as it says: 'And אליהו went to appear before אחאב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents the first side of the dispute. חזקיהו wants the prophet to come to the king, and he brings a verse as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute is about honor: who should visit whom? חזקיהו points to a precedent where a prophet, אליהו, went to a king, אחאב. So the prophet goes to the king.

phrases.english: Hezekiah said: Let Isaiah come to me,
for that is what we find with Elijah,
who went to Ahab,
as it is stated: 'And Elijah went to appear before Ahab' (I Kings 18:2).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first side of the dispute introduced in step 38.
steps.raayaObject: The prophet should go to the king.

steps.title: ישעיהו's claim: the king should come to the prophet
steps.stepSummary: ישעיהו argued that חזקיהו should come to him. His proof was that King יהורם בן אחאב went to the prophet אלישע.
steps.simpleTranslation: ישעיהו said: Let חזקיהו come to me. That is what we find with יהורם בן אחאב, who went to אלישע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents the other side of the dispute. ישעיהו brings an opposite precedent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישעיהו answers with a case that runs the other way: a king going to a prophet. Now each side has a precedent, so the dispute is stuck. That sets up God's compromise.

phrases.english: Isaiah said: Let Hezekiah come to me,
for that is what we find with Yehoram son of Ahab,
who went to Elisha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side, with a counter-precedent to step 39.
steps.raayaObject: The king should go to the prophet.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהורם בן אחאב went to אלישע (מלכים ב 3).

steps.title: God's compromise: make חזקיהו ill so ישעיהו visits him
steps.stepSummary: God made חזקיהו sick and told ישעיהו to fulfill the מצוה of ביקור חולים. So ישעיהו came to חזקיהו, but only because חזקיהו was ill. A verse proves it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did God do? He brought suffering on חזקיהו and told ישעיהו: Go and visit the sick person. As it says: 'In those days חזקיהו became deathly ill, and ישעיהו בן אמוץ the prophet came to him and said: So says the Lord of Hosts: Give orders to your household, for you will die and not live.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the compromise. God created a situation where ישעיהו had a proper reason to go to the king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side fully 'wins.' ישעיהו does go to חזקיהו, but as a visitor of the sick, not as a prophet bowing to a king. The verse from ישעיהו 38 confirms that ישעיהו came to the sick חזקיהו.

keyTerms.meaning: Give final instructions to your household

phrases.english: What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, do?
He brought suffering upon Hezekiah,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לוֹ לִישַׁעְיָהוּ: לֵךְ וּבַקֵּר אֶת הַחוֹלֶה.
phrases.english: and told Isaiah: Go and visit the sick person.
As it is stated: 'In those days Hezekiah became deathly ill,'

phrases.aramaic: וַיָּבֹא אֵלָיו יְשַׁעְיָהוּ בֶּן אָמוֹץ הַנָּבִיא
phrases.english: 'and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet came to him'

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו כֹּה אָמַר ה׳ צְבָאוֹת
phrases.english: 'and said to him: Thus says the Lord of Hosts:'

phrases.aramaic: צַו לְבֵיתֶךָ כִּי מֵת אַתָּה וְלֹא תִחְיֶה וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: 'Set your house in order, for you will die and you will not live,' etc. (Isaiah 38:1).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the stalemate between steps 39 and 40.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: God made חזקיהו ill, so ישעיהו came to him for ביקור חולים.

steps.title: Two deaths: this world and the next
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the verse says both 'you will die' and 'you will not live.' It answers: you will die in עולם הזה and not live in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'you will die and you will not live' mean? 'You will die' in this world, 'and you will not live' in the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the double wording in ישעיהו's message to חזקיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'You will die' and 'you will not live' seem to say the same thing twice. The גמרא reads them as two separate punishments: death in this world and losing עולם הבא. This makes the decree far harsher and sets up חזקיהו's shocked reaction.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'for you will die and you will not live'?
'You will die' in this world,
'and you will not live' in the World to Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the wording of the verse quoted in step 41.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the verse say the same thing twice?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One phrase refers to this world and the other to עולם הבא.

steps.title: Hezekiah asks why the punishment is so severe
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו asks ישעיהו what he did to deserve such a harsh punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיהו said to him: Why all this?
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיהו reacts to the harsh decree and asks what sin caused it. This sets up ישעיהו's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing both this world and the next is extreme, so חזקיהו wants to know the reason. The question asks for information, not a challenge to God.

keyTerms.meaning: Why all of this? / Why so much?

phrases.english: Hezekiah said to him: What is all of this?
phrases.notes: Why am I being punished so severely?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the decree explained in step 42.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What sin caused this double punishment?

steps.title: The reason: he did not have children
steps.stepSummary: ישעיהו explains that the punishment is because חזקיהו did not fulfill פריה ורביה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ישעיהו said to him: Because you did not engage in having children.
steps.whatsHappening: ישעיהו answers חזקיהו's question and names the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sin is not doing something: חזקיהו did not marry and have children. This shows how serious the מצוה of פריה ורביה is, since neglecting it can cost a person עולם הבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that פריה ורביה is so central that skipping it, even for a righteous king, brings a severe decree.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא עֲסַקְתְּ בִּפְרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה.
phrases.english: Isaiah said to him: Because you did not engage in procreation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers חזקיהו's question in step 43.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חזקיהו did not fulfill פריה ורביה.

steps.title: חזקיהו's defense: he foresaw wicked children
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו defends himself. Through רוח הקודש he saw that his children would not be good, so he chose not to have any.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיהו said to him: Because I saw through רוח הקודש that the children who come from me will not be worthy.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיהו defends his choice against ישעיהו's charge. He explains that he had a good reason not to have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיהו doesn't deny that he skipped the מצוה. He argues that his choice was justified, because he saw that his children would be wicked. (His son מנשה did turn out wicked.) The response to this defense comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Who are not worthy / not good

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the end of the story. חזקיהו's defense will be answered in the next lines. Don't assume his reason is accepted.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִשּׁוּם דַּחֲזַאי לִי בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
phrases.english: Hezekiah said to him: Because I saw through divine inspiration
that the children who will come from me will not be virtuous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends against the charge in step 44.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Not having children was a sin with no excuse.
steps.terutzMaskana: חזקיהו claims he had good reason: he foresaw that his children would be wicked.

steps.title: ישעיהו rejects חזקיהו's excuse: do your duty and leave God's secrets to God
steps.stepSummary: ישעיהו rejects חזקיהו's defense. What God will do in the future is God's business. A person's job is to keep the מצוה he was given.
steps.simpleTranslation: ישעיהו said to him: Why are you getting involved in God's hidden secrets? You were commanded to do something, and you had to do it. Whatever God wants to happen, let Him do it.
steps.whatsHappening: ישעיהו pushes back on חזקיהו's excuse from step 45 and says it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיהו said he skipped פריה ורביה because he saw through רוח הקודש that his children would be bad. ישעיהו answers that a human being does not get to skip a מצוה because of what he thinks God's future plans are. Our job is to obey. The outcome belongs to God.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key idea: a person cannot cancel a clear מצוה because he thinks the results will be bad. Doing the מצוה is our part, and the results are up to God.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בַּהֲדֵי כַּבְשֵׁי דְרַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לָךְ?
phrases.english: He (Isaiah) said to him: Why do you involve yourself with the secrets of the Merciful One?
What you were commanded, you needed to do,
phrases.notes: Referring to the מצוה of פריה ורביה.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה דְנִיחָא קַמֵּיהּ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא — לַעֲבֵיד.
phrases.english: and whatever is pleasing before the Holy One, Blessed be He, let Him do.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בַּהֲדֵי כַּבְשֵׁי דְרַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects חזקיהו's defense from step 45.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects using prophetic foresight as a reason to skip פריה ורביה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A person may not override a clear command based on God's hidden plans. Those plans are God's concern, not ours.

steps.title: חזקיהו offers to marry ישעיהו's daughter
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו accepts the point and tries to fix the problem. He asks to marry ישעיהו's daughter, hoping that both their merits together will produce worthy children.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיהו said to him: Now give me your daughter as a wife. Maybe my merit and your merit together will cause good children to come from me.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיהו stops defending himself and tries to repair the situation by offering to get married now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He no longer argues that he was right. Instead he suggests a solution: the extra merit of ישעיהו's family might change the outcome he foresaw, so his children would turn out good.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַשְׁתָּא הַב לִי בְּרַתָּךְ,
phrases.english: He (Hezekiah) said to him: Now give me your daughter,
perhaps my merit and your merit will cause it,
and worthy children will come out from me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַשְׁתָּא הַב לִי בְּרַתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After accepting ישעיהו's rejection, חזקיהו proposes a remedy.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical remedy: fix the sin by doing the מצוה now, with extra merit added.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sin of not having children is permanent, and the bad outcome is unavoidable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Marrying now, with combined merit, might bring good children and undo the punishment.

steps.title: ישעיהו: the decree is already sealed
steps.stepSummary: ישעיהו rejects the remedy. The decree of death has already been issued.
steps.simpleTranslation: ישעיהו said to him: The decree against you has already been decreed.
steps.whatsHappening: ישעיהו turns down חזקיהו's offer and says it is too late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ישעיהו's view, the time to fix things has passed. The judgment is final, so marrying now will not change it. This sets up חזקיהו's strong reaction in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: ישעיהו is not saying marriage is bad. He is saying the punishment is already set, so this fix comes too late.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּבָר נִגְזְרָה עָלֶיךָ גְּזֵירָה.
phrases.english: He (Isaiah) said to him: A decree has already been decreed against you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּבָר נִגְזְרָה עָלֶיךָ גְּזֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects חזקיהו's proposed remedy from step 47.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the remedy completely, because the decree is final.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The remedy comes after the judgment was already sealed.

steps.title: חזקיהו sends ישעיהו away
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו tells ישעיהו to finish his prophecy and leave. He refuses to accept that the decree is final.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיהו said to him: Son of אמוץ, finish your prophecy and go out!
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיהו rejects ישעיהו's claim that nothing can be done. He sends him away, and in the next step he will explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישעיהו delivered God's message, and חזקיהו accepts that part. But he does not accept ישעיהו's added opinion that there is no hope. That is why he says: finish your prophecy and leave. This is a setup line for the tradition he quotes next.
steps.confusionAlert: חזקיהו is not disrespecting a prophet's message. He accepts the prophecy itself. He only rejects the idea that prayer cannot change it.

phrases.english: He (Hezekiah) said to him: Son of Amoz,
finish your prophecy and leave!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects ישעיהו's claim from step 48 that the decree cannot be changed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the idea that the decree is final. The prophecy itself is accepted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A decree does not shut the door on prayer for mercy.

steps.title: Family tradition: never stop praying, even with a sword on your neck
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו backs up his position with a tradition from his ancestor דוד המלך: a person should never give up on asking for God's mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what I received from the house of my father's father: even if a sharp sword is resting on a person's neck, he should not hold himself back from praying for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיהו explains why he will not give up. He quotes a tradition passed down from דוד המלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tradition says that even when death seems certain, like a sword already at your neck, you should keep praying. So even a sealed decree is not a reason to stop asking God for mercy. This is the proof for his rejection in step 49.

keyTerms.meaning: I have received as a tradition
the house of my father's father (דוד המלך)

phrases.english: Thus I have received from the house of my father's father,
phrases.notes: From דוד המלך, founder of חזקיהו's royal line.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ חֶרֶב חַדָּה מוּנַּחַת עַל צַוָּארוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: even if a sharp sword is resting on a person's neck,
he should not hold himself back from asking for mercy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for חזקיהו's refusal in step 49.
steps.raayaObject: That a person may keep praying even after a decree has been issued.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A family tradition from דוד המלך.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and רבי אליעזר teach the same principle from a verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds support: רבי יוחנן and רבי אליעזר both taught the same rule. They learn it from the verse in איוב, 'Though He slay me, I will hope in Him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught that רבי יוחנן and רבי אליעזר both said: even if a sharp sword is resting on a person's neck, he should not hold himself back from praying for mercy, as the verse says: 'Though He slay me, I will hope in Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps out of the story and shows that the אמוראים taught the same principle, with a verse as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אתמר נמי' means the same idea was also stated elsewhere. Here it was stated by רבי יוחנן and רבי אליעזר. They add a פסוק from איוב: even if God is about to kill me, I still put my hope in Him. This turns חזקיהו's family tradition into a clear rule for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also stated (introduces supporting teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: No matter how hopeless things look, even with a sword on your neck or after a decree is issued, a person should never stop praying to God for mercy.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a foundational principle about תפילה that is quoted constantly: despair is never a reason to stop praying.

phrases.english: It was also stated,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Eliezer, who both said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ חֶרֶב חַדָּה מוּנַּחַת עַל צַוָּארוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: even if a sharp sword is resting on a person's neck,
he should not hold himself back from asking for mercy.
as it says: 'Though He slay me, I will hope in Him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר נָמֵי, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the tradition in step 50 with a teaching of אמוראים and a verse.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that one never stops praying for mercy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן and רבי אליעזר, based on the verse in איוב 13:15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One should never give up on prayer, even when death seems certain.
